segment: Pragmatism as a Theory of Truth

notes.title: Men Believed Laws Deciphered the Thoughts of the Almighty
Human Arbitrariness Has Driven Divine Necessity from Scientific Logic
Ideas Become True Just in So Far as They Help Us
Following the Example of Geologists, Biologists and Philologists

hard_calls: Statement 'Thus human arbitrariness has driven divine necessity from scientific logic.' is a one-sentence note; kept separate as the thesis drawn from the two notes before it, since it needs no name-span repair.
Statements 2 and 1 kept together because 'this subject' in statement 2 refers to inductive logic.
Statement 'It means, they say...' kept with the Schiller and Dewey statements because 'It' refers to 'truth' there and no source name repairs it in isolation.

Footnote pairs for 'Messrs.' / 'Schiller and Dewey...' and the 'observable in operation' / 'and then to generalize it' sentence halves are each one statement split by the stage 1 notes, so each pair stays in one note.
The last note opens with 'this general conception of all truth', which points to earlier notes; left unedited since the sentence's subject is named.
